parts.label: a
parts.technique: Conservation of linear momentum (collision)
parts.reason: This part requires conservation of momentum for a collision between two particles. No statement in the spec list mentions momentum, collision, or conservation of momentum (CLM); mechanics statements cover forces, Newton's laws, kinematics, moments, but momentum/impulse concepts are absent.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Impulse-momentum equation
parts.reason: Requires impulse = change in momentum. 'Impulse' and 'momentum' are not mentioned in any 9MA0 statement provided; only force, weight, moments, Newton's laws are covered, so this is out.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Moments/equilibrium of rigid body (non-uniform rod on two supports)
parts.reason: M9.1 explicitly covers 'moments in simple static contexts' and 'equilibrium of rigid bodies', with guidance mentioning problems with parallel coplanar forces - resolving vertically for reaction forces on a rod is standard here.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Taking moments to find centre of mass position on rod
parts.reason: M9.1 covers moments in simple static contexts including finding an unknown position via taking moments about a point; this is a standard rigid-body moments problem.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Resolving forces perpendicular to inclined plane
parts.reason: M8.2 covers situations where forces need to be resolved, extended by guidance to 'a particle moving on an inclined plane'. Resolving to find normal reaction is standard.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Friction F ≤ μR on inclined plane, resolving parallel to plane
parts.reason: M8.6 explicitly covers the F ≤ μR model for friction, coefficient of friction, and motion on rough surface, including limiting friction; resolving parallel to plane on incline is standard.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Sketching speed-time graph
parts.reason: M7.2 explicitly covers understanding, using and interpreting graphs in kinematics for motion in a straight line, including velocity-time graphs.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Constant acceleration formulae (suvat)
parts.reason: M7.3 covers use and derivation of constant acceleration formulae for straight-line motion; finding time from v=u+at is standard.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Area under velocity-time graph / suvat to find total distance and time
parts.reason: M7.2 covers interpretation of area under velocity-time graph as distance; combined with M7.3 suvat equations, this multi-stage kinematics problem is fully covered.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: suvat: v²=u²+2as under gravity
parts.reason: M7.3/M8.3 cover constant acceleration formulae and motion under gravity in a straight line; g assumed constant per M8.3, exactly this scenario.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: suvat: s=ut+1/2at² solving quadratic in t
parts.reason: Standard constant acceleration equation application under gravity, covered by M7.3/M8.3; solving resulting quadratic is P2.3 (in spec pure algebra).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Newton's second law with resistive force to find deceleration/distance (alternative: work-energy)
parts.reason: The mark scheme's main method uses N2L (F=ma) with a resistive force to find deceleration then suvat, both fully covered by M8.2/M7.3. Although an alternative work-energy method is offered, the primary N2L method is itself in spec and can score full marks, so this is IN regardless of work-energy exclusion concerns.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Finding bearing from velocity vector components
parts.reason: P10.2 covers converting between component form and magnitude/direction form of vectors; finding a bearing from i-j components is a standard vector application, extended by M7.3 guidance to vector kinematics contexts.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Position vector as function of time (constant velocity)
parts.reason: M7.3 guidance explicitly covers suvat with vectors in i-j form, e.g. r=ut+... ; writing s in terms of t for constant velocity is a direct application (with u=0 acceleration).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Vector subtraction and magnitude to find distance between two position vectors
parts.reason: P10.4 explicitly covers position vectors and calculating distance between two points given as position vectors; finding |s-b| is a direct application.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Equating vector components (due north condition) then finding magnitude
parts.reason: Uses same position vector and magnitude techniques (P10.2, P10.4) applied to a geometric condition (equal i-components for 'due north'), which is standard vector work explicitly in spec.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Newton's second law for connected particles (system) with resistances
parts.reason: M8.4 explicitly covers 'application to problems involving smooth pulleys and connected particles' and connected particle problems generally including rods; resolving for the whole system under N2L is standard.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: suvat v=u+at
parts.reason: Direct application of constant acceleration formula, covered by M7.3.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: N2L on individual particle to find tension in connecting rod
parts.reason: M8.4 covers connected particle problems (rod) and finding internal forces (tension) using Newton's second law on one particle.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: N2L for deceleration then suvat for distance
parts.reason: Combination of M8.2 (N2L, resolving with resistance forces) and M7.3 (suvat v²=u²+2as) to find deceleration and distance, both explicitly in spec.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: N2L on individual particle to find thrust in rod
parts.reason: M8.4 explicitly covers connected particle problems including rods, and finding internal force (thrust) via N2L on one particle is a direct extension of this content.
